column1: # Spoken clips, in the order of enum class Clip in include/voice.h (the host test checks both).
# Tab-separated: id, spoken text, on-screen caption, source, and optionally "heard as".
#   id        file name in assets/voice and symbol in src/voice_data.cpp
#   spoken    what the speech engine is given; spell names the way they sound
#   caption   what the screen shows while the clip plays (ASCII, at most 47 characters)
#   source    tts = synthesized by tools/generate_voice.py; legacy = an older recording, re-encoded
#   heard as  other spellings of exactly the same sounds, separated by |, that the read-back
#             check accepts (a recogniser writes "glass is" for "glasses"). Not for near misses.
# Wording notes: "spotted" survives the pitch shift far better than "nearby", and nothing says
# After editing: python tools/generate_voice.py --asr --only <id>, then commit assets/voice and
# src/voice_data.cpp together. Clips differ a little on every run, so they are kept in git.
